summary:
# NOTES ON THE THREE BOOKS (for later question-answering; use instead of source text)

## BOOK 1 — "The Datchet Diamonds" by Richard Marsh (Gutenberg 40353)
Illustrated by Stanley L. Wood. Frontispiece: "Shall I shoot all three of you?" (p.265). Chapters: I Two Men and a Maid; II Overheard in the Train; III The Diamonds; IV Miss Wentworth's Rudeness; V In the Bodega; VI The Adventures of a Night; VII Datchet Diamonds Placed in Safe Custody; VIII In the Moment of His Success; IX A Proposal of Marriage; X Cyril's Friend; XI John Ireland's Warrant; XII A Woman Roused; XIII The Detective and the Lady; XIV Among Thieves; XV Put to the Question; XVI A Modern Instance of an Ancient Practice; XVII The Most Dangerous Foe of All; XVIII The Last of the Datchet Diamonds; XIX A Woman's Logic.

**Characters:** Daisy Strong (Miss Strong; lives Medina Villas, Brighton; ~£120/yr from late mother; works for Fashion? not exactly—Charlie writes "copy" for *Fashion*). Cyril Paxton (City speculator; "punts"; lost on Eries; bought 10,000 Trumpit Gold Mine shares, bought at discount, later £10–£12 10s). Charlotte "Charlie" Wentworth (Miss Wentworth, 30, journalist, pince-nez, earns >£500/yr, sharp tongue). Mr. Lawrence (blue eyes, soft voice; real name Reginald Hargraves, alias "The Toff"; thief). The German-American / "the Baron" (Isaac Bergstein; tall, thin, stoop, huge hat & overcoat, claw-nail, clawlike hand, "eh?"). Mr. Franklyn (lawyer, ~40, grey-streaked hair, Cyril's friend, holds his shares in strongbox). John Ireland (Scotland Yard detective; bets Franklyn £100 at evens Paxton has guilty knowledge). George Hollier (officer shadowing). Skittles (thug with pail). Bill Cooper (informant, "Bill", "Tom the Toff", "the Baron"). Treadwater (Makell's Hotel manager). Stephen Eversleigh (duchess's manservant, short-sighted, gold-cased spectacles). Duchess of Datchet; Duke of Datchet. Bartlett's Bank. Chancery Lane Deposit Company safe.

**Events:** Devil's Dyke meeting in April (umbrella, Mr. Lawrence). Masonic Ball at the Dome; Miss Strong danced 5 times with Lawrence. Pier quarrel: Cyril goes "a bull on Eries"; Daisy says she will leave if he loses. Train: Paxton overhears Lawrence and Baron; Eversleigh swapped despatch-box via duplicate spectacle case (photographed by a friend). Paxton, at Brighton station refreshment room, takes Lawrence's brown new Gladstone by mistake; finds diamonds (Amsterdam Necklace, Datchet Tiara, Begum's Brooch, Banee's Bracelet; value £250,000) in bag. Fixed to Daisy: marriage within a month. Miss Wentworth quarrels with Paxton ("dishonest"). Bodega: Ireland, Lawrence & Baron confront; "What was the colour of your Gladstone bag, eh?" Night at Makell's: attempted entry by ladder; Paxton shoots at man (revolver). Next day diamonds deposited in Chancery Lane safe. Paxton trip: shadow in hotel; Trumpit shares rise to £10. Paxton drugged/kidnapped by Lawrence's men; tied; burned with branding iron "THIEF"; Paxton overpowers, Lawrence knocked out; house fired; Paxton locked in cupboard, shouts, wrote will "I give and bequeath all... to Daisy Strong... God bless her!—CYRIL PAXTON." Rescued by Daisy, Ireland's party. Trial: Lawrence & Baron each 20 years penal servitude. Paxton sells Trumpits, invests in consols; marries Daisy in Brighton church. "God grant that I may never again be led into such temptation!"

---

## BOOK 2 — "Dr. Rumsey's Patient: A Very Strange Story" by L. T. Meade & Dr. Halifax (Gutenberg 34545; Hurst & Co., 1896)
Chapters I–XVI (roman numerals with CHAPTER headings), ending "THE END."

**Characters:** Horace Frere (undergraduate, Balliol; quick-tempered; killed). Frank Everett (undergraduate, flannels; Hetty's suitor; innocent; convicted, 14 years penal servitude, Portland; mother Mrs. Everett, widow, white hair, dark eyes, obsessed with proving innocence). Hetty Armitage (innkeeper's niece at the Red Doe, Grandcourt; beautiful, black curls; later Mrs. Vincent). Robert (Robert Awdrey, Squire of The Court, Grandcourt; Balliol; cursed family "doom": memory-loss phase). Margaret Douglas (cousin of Sir John Cuthbert of Cuthbertstown; later Mrs. Awdrey). Mrs. Fanny Armitage (aunt; Perry family cooks). John Armitage (uncle, innkeeper). Ann (Awdrey sister, later Mrs. Henessey), Dorothy (sister). Dr. Arthur Rumsey (Harley Street brain specialist, unmarried). Arthur Awdrey (son, died of pneumonia, age ~4). George Vincent (farmer, Gables Farm; Hetty's husband; "Het"). Susan (dairy maid), Dan (man), Rover (dog), Susan. Payton Orr... (no, that is Book 3). Hawkins (butler). Mrs. Burnett (housekeeper). Edward Cowley (specialist). Mrs. Martin; Griffiths (steward). Jim (old prize-fighter taught stick-as-bayonet).

**Events:** Everett & Frere at Red Doe; Hetty flirts; Frere kisses Hetty by brook; Awdrey intervenes; Hetty says she loves Awdrey ("It's the Squire"). Night on Salisbury Plain: Frere and Awdrey fight; Awdrey jabs Frere's eye with stick (ferrule into brain); Awdrey buries/tosses stick in alder copse, later Hetty & aunt weight stick and sink it in pond. Awdrey forgets. Hetty and aunt swear on Testament. Picnic: Awdrey proposes to Margaret. Hetty tells Awdrey she saw murder, blames Everett. Coroner's inquest; trial at Salisbury; verdict guilty, mercy recommended; 14 years. Margaret & Awdrey marry; son Arthur born; Grandcourt. Mrs. Everett visits Rumsey; visits Hetty (now Mrs. Vincent) on Plain. Rumsey treats Awdrey; night sleep at Rumsey's; sketch of murder scene. Arthur (child) dies of pneumonia. Awdrey forgets child. Awdrey goes to Grandcourt with Rumsey; sees reflection in pond, remembers murder; "It was your own face." Hetty visits Awdrey in London and Grandcourt; Hetty drugs husband Vincent with laudanum in stout; he dies. Hetty confesses to Awdrey in office; Awdrey confesses publicly in drawing room; Hetty dies of heart failure after giving deposition. Everett pardoned by Home Secretary; Awdrey acquitted at Salisbury ("Not Guilty"). Closing: Margaret: "You can be a thousand times better."

---

## BOOK 3 — "When Oriole Traveled Westward" by Amy Bell Marlowe (Gutenberg 76223; Grosset & Dunlap, 1921; sequel to "When Oriole Came to Harbor Light")
Chapters I–XXX: I An Adventure on the Ice; II Teddy Ford; III Strange Actions; IV Oriole Is Worried; V What Happened in the Night; VI Teddy Ford's Story; VII Other People's Troubles; VIII Oriole's Own Troubles; IX A Great Change Coming; X Partings; XI A Great Deal That Is New; XII Exciting Times; XIII At the Range Camp; XIV Ching Foo; XV Molly; XVI The Spring Round-Up; XVII The Bird of Freedom; XVIII A New Deal; XIX An Exciting Fishing Party; XX Bruin on the Line; XXI News of Moment; XXII Something Going On; XXIII Suspicion Is Rife; XXIV The Twins in Trouble; XXV Nature's Wonders; XXVI At Close Quarters; XXVII The Wrist Watch; XXVIII Shall Oriole Be Told?; XXIX Of Course!; XXX The Promise of the Future.

**Characters:** Oriole Putnam (Brazilian-raised, from Bahia; parents Mr. Noddy-"Noddy" Putnam & Mrs. Putnam; "Sister" was mother's nickname for her). Myron & Marian Langdon (4-yr-old twins; "Mawyann" = Marian). Harvey Langdon (Montana ranchman; Three-bar Ranch; Mr. Langdon). Sadie "Brownie" Brown (twins' nurse, Western, brusque). Teddy Ford (curly brown hair, grins; "Gee!"; runaway, accused of stealing Langdon silver chest; father a prospector, died). Nat Jardin (lightkeeper, Harbor Light Island; rheumatism) & Ma Stafford (housekeeper). Lyddy Ann (maid at Mrs. Rebecca Joy's, Dexter Mansion, State Street, Littleport). Mrs. Joy (sea-captain's widow). Payton Orr (substitute lightkeeper, gossip). Anson Cope (iceboat *Bluebird*). Shedder Crabbe (son of Enos Crabbe, storekeeper/Town Council president; ram Jingo). Minnie & Flossy Payne; May Rabey; Busy Bees society. Billy Bragg (cabin boy, *Adrian Marple*). Ching Foo (Canton cook; pidgin: "Plenty bad mans here..."; "Three topside bad men"). Sol Perkins (ranch manager). George Belden (trail foreman; married Sadie Brown later). Hank Ridley (Tony/Hank; black-mustached, red-faced; chief outlaw), Shaffer (mouse-colored hair, brown coat), Tom Mudd. Lenny, Long Jim (cowboys). Molly (blue pony). Blooey (lazy pony). Doctor Simms. Abel Hubbard (factotum, Brick Hotel). Captain Nathan Grimsby, Mrs. Grimsby, ship *Ellerton* (three-masted, traded South Seas). *Helvetia* (British steamship); *Adrian Marple*; *Portland* steamboat; Camper Reef.

**Events:** Oriole drags twins on sled to Harbor Light Island; iceboat *Bluebird* breaks ice; Oriole & twins fall in; Teddy rescues Marian & others. Teddy angry at Langdon, runs away at night. Lyddy Ann "ghost" sheet; Enos Crabbe chased by Jingo. Surprise party for Oriole. Langdon learns of mother's possible rescue (ship *Ellerton*); father drowned. Departure by train West; Oriole sees Teddy in stock car (horses) at Chicago-side siding; he promises "by the spring round-up." Round-up; Oriole's cow-branding, mad cow; Molly. Teddy saves Myron from eagle with lariat; Langdon apologizes ("This is a new deal"). Oriole overhears Ridley/Mudd/Shaffer talk of "prospect hole" near "Three Sisters." Squaw Canyon fishing trip; bear caught on fishline. Stolen horses (22) recovered. Ridley & Mudd abduct twins; Myron seen on cliff across waterfall; Oriole discovers path behind waterfall. Shaffer caught fighting Mudd; Belden's posse arrives. Oriole's wrist watch (from Myron) lost. Oriole unties rope in prospect hole; Ridley trapped. Ridley rescued; Teddy finds stolen silver chest wrapped in horse blanket. Mrs. Putnam found alive on ship *Ellerton*; telegram "Leave by overland special... Meet me at Timmins Station.—Mother." Langdon promises replacement watch.
